note: Selective Kv1.5/IKur blockers (S9947, MK-0448, XEN-D0101/0103 = S66913, BMS-914392/919373) prolonged atrial refractoriness and stopped AF in pig, goat and dog models, but the human atrium barely answered: MK-0448 moved nothing at >2 µmol/L and XEN-D0103/S66913 left AF burden unchanged in two trials; vernakalant is a mixed-channel relative and is excluded.
label: AF (Kv1.5 blockers)

engagement.note: Selective IKur blockers S9947/S20951 prolonged atrial but not ventricular refractoriness in pigs — the pharmacodynamic readout the class carried into humans.
engagement.short: IKur block prolongs pig atrial ERP
engagement.quote: In contrast to I(Kr) blockade, I(Kur) blockade had no effect on the QT-interval, but prolonged the atrial ERP.

engagement.note: MK-0448 prolonged dog AERP, but healthy volunteers showed no atrial refractoriness change at >2 µmol/L plasma — the pharmacodynamic marker never moved.
engagement.short: No human AERP change at >2 µM
engagement.quote: During the electrophysiological study, ascending doses of MK-0448 were administered, but no increases in atrial or ventricular refractoriness were detected, despite achieving plasma concentrations in excess of 2 μmol/L.
engagement.reason: Dog AERP effect absent in humans
engagement.judgement: AERP is the class's pharmacodynamic surrogate for Kv1.5 block (as sweat chloride is for CFTR), so a null AERP at >2 µmol/L is scored as engagement contra, not only dose. Patient atrial tissue ex vivo (Loose 2014, doi:10.3389/fphar.2014.00026) shows MK-0448 does block Kv1.5 in human atrium but shortens APD90/ERP in sinus-rhythm tissue and prolongs it only in permanent-AF tissue — the mechanism of the miss. No ClinicalTrials.gov record was found for the MK-0448 first-in-human study (searched by drug name, sponsor Merck + AF, and Kv1.5/IKur terms). BMS-919373's pacemaker AERP study (NCT02153437, first posted 2014-06-03) was terminated at n=7 with no results posted.

dose.note: IKur blockers TAEA/ISQ-1 raised dog AERP 16% at 59–330 nM plasma and terminated AF in failing dogs at ~0.7–0.8 µM.
dose.quote: In anesthetized dogs, i.v. infusions of TAEA and ISQ-1 elicited comparable 16% increases in atrial refractory period, with no effect on ventricular refractory period or QTc interval.

dose.note: Human plasma MK-0448 exceeded 2 µmol/L, beyond the dog-effective range, yet atrial refractoriness did not budge; vagal tone in dogs reproduced the loss.
dose.quote: The contribution of I(Kur) to human atrial electrophysiology is less prominent than in preclinical models and therefore is likely to be of limited therapeutic value for the prevention of atrial fibrillation.
dose.reason: Dog exposure target failed in humans
dose.judgement: Same study as the engagement cell, scored separately because the abstract states the animal-derived exposure target was met and exceeded (>2 µmol/L) without effect. Regan 2008's dog concentrations are for the class proxies TAEA and ISQ-1, not MK-0448; the MK-0448 dog concentration–response sits in the paywalled full text, so magnitude is recorded as direction-only.

efficacy.note: S9947/S20951 abolished pacing-induced left-atrial tachyarrhythmias in pigs; goat persistent-AF (2004) and failing-dog AF (2008) models later agreed.
efficacy.short: IKur block stops pig atrial arrhythmia
efficacy.quote: The I(Kur) blockers, S20951and S9947, significantly decreased left atrial vulnerability (-82% and -100%, respectively, P<0.01) in contrast to the selective I(Kr) blocker dofetilide (-14%; n.s.).
efficacy.confidence: high (abstract; quote reproduces the abstract's missing space in 'S20951and')

efficacy.model: Patient atrial trabeculae ex vivo + pig/goat/dog AF models
efficacy.note: XEN-D0103 prolonged patient atrial APs at high rates ex vivo and animal models predicted efficacy, but AF burden was unchanged (ratio 1.01, p=0.77).
efficacy.quote: XEN-D0103 did not reduce AF burden in patients with PAF and dual chamber pacemakers providing beat-to-beat monitoring.
efficacy.confidence: medium (abstract + EU-CTR results record; full text not read, so whether the discussion itself compares to the preclinical prediction is unverified)
efficacy.reason: No AF-burden effect in two trials
efficacy.judgement: Two independent negative trials of the same molecule: Shunmugam 2018 (Xention, n=21 crossover, pacemaker Holter; EU-CTR 2013-004456-38 results first published 2016-07-09: AF-burden ratio of geometric means 1.01, 90% CI 0.98–1.05, p=0.77) and S66913/DIAGRAF-IKUR (Servier, n=58, insertable monitor, 5/25/100 mg; doi:10.1093/ehjcvp/pvy022, print 2019; EU-CTR 2014-002333-63 results first published 2017-06-02; 'no significant effect on AFB' at any dose, stopped for an unspecified non-clinical safety concern). The model named is the XEN-D0103 pivotal preclinical paper (Ford 2016, doi:10.1016/j.hrthm.2015.10.003: APD prolongation at high rates in SR/pAF trabeculae 'could be of therapeutic benefit for reducing AF burden'), standing on the pig (Knobloch 2002), goat (Blaauw 2004, doi:10.1161/01.CIR.0000143050.22291.2E, AVE0118 — mixed IKur/Ito) and failing-dog (Regan 2008) AF models; I juxtaposed model and trial myself. The 2002→2018 strip hides that no efficacy trial was run between: MK-0448 never reached one because its PD failed (2012). BMS-919373 phase 2 (NCT02156076, rabbit + dog PD models per Gunaga 2017 doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b01889) was terminated for business reasons; results posted 2019-05-22 state 'Data was not collected for any participants'. BMS-914392 phase 2 (NCT01356914) completed 2012 with no results posted and no publication found. Vernakalant excluded as mixed-channel.

safety.note: Pigs predicted atrial selectivity: IKur blockers left QTc untouched while IKr blockers prolonged it.
safety.quote: In contrast to selective I(Kr) blockade, I(Kur) blockade inhibited left atrial vulnerability and had no effect on the QT-interval.

safety.note: Dogs and healthy volunteers alike showed no ventricular refractoriness change; XEN-D0101/0103 later added no QTc effect up to 7000 ng/mL.
safety.short: No ventricular effect in dogs or humans
safety.quote: During the electrophysiological study, ascending doses of MK-0448 were administered, but no increases in atrial or ventricular refractoriness were detected, despite achieving plasma concentrations in excess of 2 μmol/L.
safety.judgement: Weak match: the human ventricular silence is less informative because the atrial effect was absent too. Corroboration: Ford 2016 (doi:10.1016/j.hrthm.2015.10.003) pairs no effect on human ventricular action potentials at 10 µM with no ΔΔQTcF at plasma levels up to 7000 ng/mL in volunteers (comparison stated in the source); Ford 2013 (doi:10.1097/FJC.0b013e31828780eb) reports XEN-D0101 did not raise QTc to 300 mg; Shunmugam 2018 and the S66913 trial report no serious adverse events in patients. The S66913 programme was stopped for a 'non-clinical safety concern' that neither the paper nor EU-CTR 2014-002333-63 describes — unknown whether any model flagged it, and nothing it flagged has been published.
